paper.title: Algorithm 816: r2d2lri: an algorithm for automatic two-dimensional cubature
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 28(1), Mar 2002, p. 75-100 (per the shipped 816 shar header and the frame item). The ACM article was not fetched.
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/816.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 816.gz (shell archive; C++/Dp/Src/r2d2lri.h and r2d2lri.cpp; C++/Dp/Drivers/r2d2lri_sample.cpp and res; Doc/Readme.txt)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/816.gz (66691 bytes). Unpacked with /bin/sh in an empty directory /tmp/scout-414-bOZh/x; no build or run by scout.
code.note: Unpack 816.gz with gunzip, then run the shar with /bin/sh in an empty directory. Build C++/Dp/Src/r2d2lri.cpp with C++/Dp/Drivers/r2d2lri_sample.cpp using any C++ compiler (record it). Run the sample and compare the block 'Requested accuracy = 6 significant figures' with the shipped res file. The rerun must not change the requested accuracy or the integrand. The 'I1' block and the 2-, 4- and 10-figure blocks are not part of the claim.

field: numerics (two-dimensional adaptive cubature for an improper integral)

claim.location: C++/Dp/Drivers/res inside 816.gz: block 'COMPUTATION OF I30 TO 2, 4, 6 AND 10 FIGURES', the block for 'Requested accuracy = 6 significant figures': 'The computed value of I30 is 3.14159259152384e+00'. The integrand is the one in the header of that block, I30 = integral over [0,inf) of dy dx / (sqrt(-xy) (y-x+1)^2) as printed by r2d2lri_sample.cpp.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: The ACM article was not read; the claim is the code's own shipped reference output, not a value located in the paper.
claim.metric: The computed value of I30 printed for requested accuracy 6 significant figures, compared as an absolute number with the value the rerun prints in the same block.
claim.determinism: deterministic (adaptive quadrature with fixed inputs and no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped value is printed with 15 digits, so print rounding is negligible. The shipped value itself is 2.0e-8 relative from pi, and the requested accuracy is 1e-6 relative. A rerun of the same algorithm may differ by floating-point rounding, which should be well under 1e-8. A different adaptive path that stops early changes the value by more than 1e-8. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: compile two C++ files and run the sample (about 32000 integrand evaluations in total across the four accuracy levels).
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive (ACM TOMS collected algorithm); the rerun should record the archive's licence notice.

why: The sample runs the automatic adaptive cubature on a singular improper two-dimensional integral and reports a value whose exact path depends on the implemented error estimator; the number is not a closed form that could be checked on paper.
